claim: Moving rules from memory into the medium (physically enforced or visible) lowers errors and time in an isomorphic puzzle; all errors fell on internal rules (Tower of Hanoi isomorphs, N=18, 24).
agent_test: Same puzzle with rules stated in prose vs enforced by a code validator that rejects illegal moves; equal tokens; count rule violations and solve rate.

claim: Isomorphic problems (same logic, different surface and encoding) differ greatly in difficulty for people and for LLMs; models prefer text over image forms of the same problem (Claude-3 Opus 28.7 pts worse on images, GPT-4 Turbo 18.7, Gemini Pro 14.9).
agent_test: Build 3-5 isomorphic phrasings of 30 held-out items; report pass rate range per phrasing at equal tokens; pick the form on a held-out split.
audit_note: Minor: the human-difficulty part rests on Zhang & Norman's Tower of Hanoi isomorphs (qualitative discussion, e.g. II-E23 much easier than ZI23); IsoBench deltas (28.7/18.7/14.9) verified.

claim: Having the model write the state as a text grid after each step helps spatial tasks for a strong model (GPT-4 tiling 63.94 vs 54.15 CoT; route success 14.72 vs 9.48), but not on arithmetic-reducible ring navigation (49.5 vs 52.5, N=200) and not for weak models (GPT-3.5 9.00 vs 8.50).
agent_test: VoT-style state grid vs plain CoT on our grid items at equal tokens, with a code check of each drawn state.

claim: In Visualization-of-Thought the drawn state is often wrong (state accuracy 26.48% navigation / 24.25% tiling; constraint compliance 51.14% / 52.01%), while decisions given an accurate drawing were right 65.16% / 77.20% of the time, so drawing accuracy is the bottleneck; in MVoT, 90.80% of text-CoT errors on FrozenLake were wrong hole coordinates in the written state (fine-tuned Anole-7B CoT: 0.9401 at 3x3 down to 0.3911 at 6x6). Whether code verification of the written state would fix this is untested in these sources.
agent_test: Compare free-form sketch vs sketch checked and corrected by code; measure state accuracy and final accuracy.
audit_note: Numbers verified (VoT compliance 51.14/52.01, state accuracy 26.48/24.25, decision accuracy given correct drawing 65.16/77.20; MVoT 90.80%, CoT 0.9401 to 0.3911), but neither paper tests code verification of the written state, so 'code verification is the lever' is the notes' inference; the 0.94/0.39 CoT figures are a fine-tuned Anole-7B 'CoT with env layout' row.
claim_before_audit: Self-drawn state is often wrong (state accuracy about 24-26%, constraint compliance about 51-52%); the gain depends on drawing accuracy, so code verification of the written state is the lever. MVoT: 90.80% of text-CoT errors on FrozenLake were wrong hole coordinates in the written state (CoT 0.94 at 3x3, 0.39 at 6x6).

claim: A code- or tool-built representation beats the raw one: ARC object lists lifted GPT-4 from 13/50 to 23/50 (97 vs 81 of 400 on full set); executed physics simulation let a 1.3B model match a 175B one; executed sketches added about 11 points (GPT-4o) on math. Boundary: code on a noisy raw table fell 31.8% vs 20.5% for text; normalise first (TableMaster).
agent_test: ARC portfolio: raw row-text grid vs object list from code, same token budget; paired per-item comparison.
audit_note: Minor: Mind's Eye 1.3B-matches-175B is the zero-shot UTOPIA result (29.8% vs 29%); Sketchpad 11.2% is the paper's average gain for GPT-4o on math.

claim: Serialisation format changes accuracy and the best format depends on task and model: tables (HTML 83.43 vs NL+sep 73.12 size detection, GPT-4), graphs (incident 53.8 vs adjacency 19.8), prompts (up to 76 points spread, LLaMA-2-13B). Whether spread shrinks for the strongest models is contested: Sclar 2024 says sensitivity persists with size; no measurement exists on 2025-2026 reasoning models.
agent_test: Run each scaffold over 4+ meaning-preserving formats; report the range; credit a gain only if it exceeds the format noise floor.

claim: No single form wins everywhere: GPT-3.5 reverse lookup best in XML, worst in HTML; CoT hurt some graph tasks; square-grid WoT below CoT; CoT beats VoT on ring task. Whiteboard-of-Thought (GPT-4o): hexagon CoT 8 vs WoT 61, square CoT 98 vs WoT 50.
agent_test: Let the agent choose form per task class from a small pilot (AutoForm-style) and compare against a fixed form.

claim: Letting the model pick its own non-prose thought format (tables, logic, code) before reasoning gives modest gains (+5.4 GPT-3.5, +5.7 Gemini Pro, +3.3 GPT-4). A router trained once on 14,200 labelled items (Sketch-of-Thought) picks among 3 compact forms with accuracy within 1% at about 26% of CoT tokens; per-item pilot selection untested.
agent_test: Add a form-selection step; compare to fixed-prose CoT at equal total tokens (selection step counts).
audit_note: Minor: the 14,200 router training labels are machine-labelled (GPT-4o), and 'about 26% of CoT tokens' is the paper's 'over 74% average token reduction'.

claim: Adding a picture to a text description often hurts or is ignored by VLMs; models trust text over image when they conflict, and fail on simple diagram facts.
agent_test: Offer text-only vs text+image of the same state; check which wins when we plant an error in the text.

claim: Natural-frequency wording raises Bayesian performance in people (Bayesian algorithms 16% vs 46%/50% in G&H Study 1; 36% vs 68% correct in medical students N=577), visual aids add, training adds; rival explanation is nested-set structure.
agent_test: Probability vs natural-frequency vs nested-set restatement on Bayes items, several LLMs, equal tokens.
audit_note: The Gigerenzer and Hoffrage 'Bayesian algorithms 16% vs 46%/50%' figures are in none of the listed sources (the Cui et al. review gives 48% vs 22% correct for that study; I could not open the 1995 paper); the medical-student result (N=577, 36% vs 68% correct pretest, OR 11.55), visual aids, training, and the nested-sets rival account are supported.

claim: Frequency formats help LLMs on Bayesian tasks: still unmeasured. The citation chain to Dasgupta/Lampinen 2022 is a mis-citation (that paper has no Bayes or frequency test; CogBias 2026 repeats the false line). Only data: Araya 2025, one item, three reasoning models, none used natural frequencies unprompted and use was shallow when prompted.
agent_test: Direct LLM test as in K10; this is a hole in the literature.

claim: Acting on physical materials does not reliably help insight problems: 27.3% vs 32.6% (N=87), failed replications (matchstick algebra, N=105/88/74), large test found no effect except Eight Coins; positive reports used weak controls (3-6% vs 43% elsewhere).
agent_test: Do not add an act-on-it step by default; if tried, pair with a strong plain baseline.

claim: What the picture shows can matter more than action: realistic matchstick photo 79.3% vs stylised 46.7% (N=59), because it carried the key fact; also the salience of the key move in the cheap-necklace problem.
agent_test: Restate a stuck problem so the hidden constraint is explicit vs neutral restatement; compare solve rate.

claim: Output representation matters: asking for a full move list produced part of the apparent Hanoi collapse; a generator or stepwise state fixed part.
agent_test: Ask for answer as a program vs explicit list on Hanoi with N disks.

claim: Procedures learned in one representation (code, graph) do not reliably transfer to natural language in trained models.
agent_test: Prompt-only: same procedure as code vs prose on a fixed model.

claim: The Larkin-Simon claim (diagram makes inference local) has no direct LLM replication; closest analogues are incident-list graph encoding, ARC objects, VoT. Indirect analogue: answer position matters (Lost in the Middle: GPT-3.5 falls over 20 points, below closed-book 56.1%, when the fact is mid-context).
agent_test: Build an item set where relevant facts are adjacent vs scattered in text; same content; measure accuracy.

claim: No 2024-2026 paper found compares a written-state or visual-thought method with plain CoT at equal total tokens. Sketchpad reports 2.2k-3.1k tokens per math or graph sample (26.6k on V*Bench) with no matched baseline. Terse written forms keep accuracy at 20-26% of CoT tokens (Sketch-of-Thought within 1% average; Chain of Draft GSM8K 91.1 vs 95.4), so a token-capped CoT is the fair baseline.
agent_test: Run plain CoT, terse CoT capped to the same tokens, and code-checked ledger on one fixed item set; count every token including checks.

claim: Rendering choice depends on whether text has a natural coordinate form: GPT-4o on tile navigation, hexagon CoT 8 vs rendered 61, triangle 26 vs 55, circle 25 vs 41, but square 98 vs 50. Remaining rendered-image errors come mostly from perception (80.8% ceiling on real MNIST images).
agent_test: Pilot: same item as text grid and as code-rendered image; choose image only where text coordinates are not natural.

claim: Rewriting or reformatting gains depend on the baseline. Rephrase-and-Respond lifted GPT-4 from 64.95 to 89.77 average against direct zero-shot (last letter 52 to 99), but near-ceiling tasks gained 0-2 points and weaker models gained less. Its baseline had no CoT.
agent_test: Report every rewrite/format gain against plain CoT and terse CoT arms, not only direct answering.

claim: Output-structure limits hurt reasoning when they remove the thinking channel: gpt-4o-mini GSM8K 94.57 free text vs 86.95 JSON-mode vs 91.71 JSON-schema; JSON-mode put the answer before the reasoning in 100% of GPT-3.5 responses.
agent_test: Keep reasoning free-form or reason-before-answer; only structure the final answer.

claim: Hidden-constraint restatement for LLM insight puzzles is untested. BRAINTEASER tests rephrase and context swaps, not constraint reveal; ChatGPT scored about 53/63% vs human 92% (2023).
agent_test: Add a 'constraint stated' arm to the BRAINTEASER portfolio against plain and terse-CoT arms.

claim: Format spread on 2025-2026 reasoning models is unmeasured in the sources found. 2023-2024 evidence says spread persists with model size (Sclar) and with gpt-4o-mini (Tam), and Araya 2025 shows reasoning models ignore suggested solution format. Needs a measurement on our own model.
agent_test: Run 4+ meaning-preserving formats on 30 items on our model; accept a format only if its gain exceeds the spread.
